topics.label: Lecture opening and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic, sets expectations, and outlines how the content builds on previously introduced immunological concepts.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition via PAMPs and DAMPs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects infection and tissue injury through conserved molecular patterns and germline-encoded pattern recognition receptors.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families and intracellular signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine major receptor families, their downstream signaling pathways, and the assembly of the inflammasome to generate active inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how tissue sentinel cells and vascular endothelial cells coordinate to recruit and guide circulating leukocytes to the site of infection.

topics.label: Lymphatic trafficking and systemic consequences of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the dissemination of inflammatory processes beyond the local site of infection, including cell migration through lymphatics and the dangers of systemic overactivation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms that terminate acute immune reactions to enable tissue healing, as well as the pathological and protective aspects of persistent chronic inflammation.

topics.label: Lecture closing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the topic of the following session.
